## Candidate result

This unrefereed candidate gives negative answers to both global questions in Hayman–Lingham Problem 6.72 (2306072 / AMR-022-6072). Every actual global maximizer of Re[a2 + i·10^(-24)·(a4 − 3a3)] has an omitted slit with nonmonotone argument and nonmonotone radial angle. Both signed and ordinary unsigned angle conventions are covered.

The proof obtains genuine support points by compactness, bounds their slit tips, identifies the tested trajectory with their actual omitted arcs, and controls the perturbation error uniformly over all maximizers. It uses the explicitly stated classical compactness, coefficient, area, and support-slit/Schiffer theorems. It does not claim an explicit maximizing map or uniqueness.

## Verification

- Frozen candidate preserved byte-for-byte: 56 exact author checks pass.
- Full independent adversarial AI audit included: PASS, no required mathematical revisions; 23 additional exact checks pass.
- Author and audit SHA-256 manifests checked; final repository layout replayed.
- Queue change is confined to this row’s Status, Turns, and Findings: claimed_solved, 1/5.

The original frozen status records the pre-audit stage; independent-audit/AUDIT_RESULT.json and INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md record the subsequent PASS. This remains unrefereed. Historical priority and novelty are not established; an AI audit is not human peer review. The finite verifiers do not formalize the analytic inputs.

No source PDFs, corpus files, or private coordination records are included. Draft for review; no merge or release requested.
title: 2306072: candidate counterexample to support-slit monotonicity
